methodology:
Research compiled for psygrid-reports quantitative trading research. Primary sources are the issuing official bodies (Federal Reserve/FOMC, BLS, BEA, Census Bureau, ECB, Bank of England/ONS, Bank of Japan, Statistics Bureau of Japan, RBA, ABS, RBNZ, Stats NZ, Bank of Canada, Statistics Canada, National Bureau of Statistics of China, EIA, API, OPEC, IEA) wherever a date/time could be confirmed. IMPORTANT ENVIRONMENT CAVEAT: this research was conducted in a sandboxed environment whose network egress proxy blocks direct HTTP(S) fetches to essentially all government/central-bank/IEA/OPEC/API top-level domains (bls.gov, bea.gov, census.gov, federalreserve.gov, ecb.europa.eu, bankofengland.co.uk, ons.gov.uk, boj.or.jp, rba.gov.au, abs.gov.au, rbnz.govt.nz, stats.govt.nz, bankofcanada.ca, statcan.gc.ca, stats.gov.cn, eia.gov, api.org, opec.org, iea.org were all unreachable via direct fetch). All dates/times were therefore obtained via web search snippets that quote, excerpt, or index these official pages (including officially-hosted PDFs and press releases surfaced by the search engine), then cross-checked against at least one reputable secondary calendar (TradingEconomics, Investing.com, FXStreet, Forex Factory, financecalendar.com, or similar) where possible. Every event carries an official_source field naming the primary body/page and a secondary_crosscheck field naming the corroborating secondary source. exact_time_confirmed is true only when the specific date AND local release time were corroborated with reasonable confidence; it is false for events where the date and/or time is a pattern-based estimate, a commonly-cited-but-not-primary-sourced approximation, or otherwise carries meaningful uncertainty - in every such case the notes field explains the basis for the estimate and what to verify closer to the date. No date or time in this dataset was invented without basis; where no reasonable estimate could be made, the item was omitted rather than guessed. Weekly recurring series (EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, API Weekly Statistical Bulletin, U.S. Initial Jobless Claims) are itemized once per week for the whole window, with holiday-shift weeks flagged explicitly. Timezone/DST handling: all local-time-to-IST conversions were computed programmatically using IANA tzdata (Python zoneinfo) for the exact date of each event, not manually, to correctly account for DST transitions within the window: US/Canada Eastern time remains EDT (UTC-4) for the entire window (US/Canada DST does not end until Sunday Nov 1, 2026, after the window closes); Euro Area/UK time is CEST/BST (UTC+2/UTC+1) through Saturday Oct 24, 2026 and CET/GMT (UTC+1/UTC+0) from Sunday Oct 25, 2026 (DST end) onward - so events after Oct 25 sit one hour later relative to IST than an equivalent local time before Oct 25; Australia is AEST (UTC+10) through Saturday Oct 3, 2026 and AEDT (UTC+11) from Sunday Oct 4, 2026 (DST start) onward; New Zealand is NZST (UTC+12) through Saturday Sep 26, 2026 and NZDT (UTC+13) from Sunday Sep 27, 2026 (DST start) onward; Japan, China and India do not observe DST and stay at fixed UTC+9 / UTC+8 / UTC+5:30 respectively throughout. KNOWN CAVEATS: (1) A U.S. government funding lapse ("shutdown") occurred earlier in FY2026 (a DHS-related partial shutdown Feb 14 - Apr 30, 2026) following the Oct 1 2025-Nov 12 2025 shutdown that disrupted BLS/Census/BEA data collection and release schedules; as of this research (Sep 22, 2026) a continuing resolution reportedly funds the government through Dec 11, 2026, so no shutdown-driven delay to the Sep22-Oct31, 2026 window was identified, but this should be reconfirmed close to each release given the pattern of repeated 2025-2026 funding lapses. (2) BoE: the Sep 17, 2026 MPC decision is the last one before this window opens; per the official 2026 MPC schedule the next decision is Nov 5, 2026, which falls OUTSIDE this window - there is deliberately NO BoE rate-decision event in this dataset. (3) RBA: the RBA now runs an 8-meetings/year schedule; the Sep 28-29, 2026 meeting (decision Sep 29) is the only RBA decision in this window - there is NO RBA meeting in October 2026 (next is Nov 2-3, 2026, outside the window) - confirmed against the official RBA 2026 schedule. (4) Every date/time flagged exact_time_confirmed=false should be reconfirmed against the named official_source shortly before trading around it; several (UK labour market October date, Japan trade balance date, Caixin PMI post-holiday date, China trade balance date, OPEC+ JMMC time, IEA OMR exact date, BoJ decision exact minute, New Zealand CPI exact minute, Australia flash PMI, US September new home sales date) are pattern-based estimates rather than directly-sourced primary confirmations.

PRECISION AUDIT ADDENDUM (see docs/PRECISION_AUDIT.md): every event now also carries `time_confirmation_tier` (official_source_cited / secondary_calendar_only / pattern_estimate) and `event_class` (MAJOR / SECONDARY / RESEARCH_ONLY), derived mechanically from exact_time_confirmed + importance. `time_confirmation_tier=official_source_cited` means an official institutional calendar/page was the cited origin, NOT that it was fetched and read directly (this research environment could not reach any of those domains -- see original methodology note above). Treat MAJOR as the reliable engine-activation set; SECONDARY and RESEARCH_ONLY remain in the dataset for completeness and must be explicitly opted into.

events.secondary_crosscheck: Investing.com 'EIA Crude Oil Inventories' calendar entry
events.notes: Standard Wednesday 10:30am ET release (summary), full tables 1:00pm ET.

events.event_name: Monthly CPI Indicator (incl. Q3 2026 quarterly CPI), September 2026
events.official_source: ABS release pattern: quarterly CPI figures are folded into the monthly CPI release for March/June/September/December reference months
events.notes: This release is the most important Australian data point in the window: it is the monthly CPI for September AND carries the full quarterly (Q3 2026) CPI figure the RBA weights most heavily, published on the last Wednesday of October. Now in AEDT (Australian DST began Oct 4, 2026).

events.event_name: RBNZ Official Cash Rate Decision (Monetary Policy Review)
events.official_source: RBNZ 'Monetary policy decision dates ... 2026/27' official schedule page (rbnz.govt.nz/hub/news) and RBNZ events calendar entry for this date
events.notes: This is a Monetary Policy REVIEW (shorter statement, no full projections/press conference-length Monetary Policy Statement) - one of RBNZ's 3 'review-only' decisions per year, vs. 4 full Monetary Policy Statement decisions. OCR published 2:00pm NZDT, online media conference ~3:00pm NZDT. New Zealand DST (NZDT) began Sep 27, 2026, so NZ is UTC+13 for this entire event.

events.event_name: Initial Jobless Claims (weekly UI claims report)
events.official_source: U.S. Department of Labor / Employment and Training Administration weekly release schedule (oui.doleta.gov) - 8:30am ET every Thursday, shifted only around federal holidays
events.notes: Recurring weekly release. No Monday federal holiday falls in the reporting weeks covered by these Thursdays in this window, so no date shift expected (Columbus Day, Oct 12, is a Monday but does not affect the Thursday claims schedule).

events.event_name: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Decision + Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices
events.official_source: Bank of Japan 'Scheduled Dates of Monetary Policy Meetings in 2026' official PDF (boj.or.jp)
events.secondary_crosscheck: TradingEconomics, MNI BoJ Meeting Calendar, multiple secondary trackers
events.notes: Meeting is Oct 29-30 (Thu-Fri) with the decision and quarterly Outlook Report published on Day 2 (Oct 30). Exact release MINUTE is not fixed/pre-announced by the BoJ - historically the statement drops somewhere between roughly 11:20 and 13:00 JST; 12:00 JST used here is a commonly cited approximate midpoint, not an official fixed time. Press conference (Governor Ueda) is typically ~15:30 JST.
